nodes.name: Core-shell ZIF synthesis + H2 pyrolysis
nodes.procedure: A well-defined core–shell ZIF-8@ZIF-67 was prepared as the precursor (Fig. S7–S9, ESI†). Then, it was pyrolyzed under 5 mol% H2/Ar to modulate the N_[5]/N_[6] ratios via the ring-reconstruction effect catalyzed by the in situ generated Co nanoparticles (Co_n), obtaining NC with an equal ratio of N_[5]/N_[6] and Co_n loading (Co_n–N_[5]/6C).

unit_operations.name: Core-shell formation
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: well-defined core–shell ZIF-8@ZIF-67 was prepared as the precursor (Fig. S7–S9, ESI†)

nodes.source_text: Based on the above insights, a well-defined core–shell ZIF-8@ZIF-67 was prepared as the precursor... NC with an equal ratio of N_[5]/N_[6] and Co_n loading (Co_n–N_[5]/6C) was obtained by pyrolyzing of ZIF-8@ZIF-67 in 5 mol% H2/Ar.

nodes.name: Ar pyrolysis of ZIF-8@ZIF-67
nodes.procedure: Core–shell ZIF-8@ZIF-67 was pyrolyzed in pure Ar. For comparison, Co_n–N_[6]C was also prepared by pyrolyzing in pure Ar.
nodes.source_text: For comparison, Co_n–N_[6]C was also prepared by pyrolyzing in pure Ar.

nodes.name: Pt coordination confinement
nodes.procedure: Both Co_n–N_[5]/6C and Co_n–N_[6]C were constructed by coordinate-confining Pt_1 by impregnating in H2PtCl6 at 60°C.
nodes.source_text: both Co_n–Pt_1@N_[6]C and Co_n–Pt_1@N_[5]/[6]C were constructed by coordinate-confining Pt_1 by impregnating in H2PtCl6 at 60°C

nodes.description: Alkaline HER performance in 1 M KOH three-electrode system
nodes.source_text: The polarization curve in 1 M KOH reveals that Co_n–Pt_1@N_[5]/[6]C demonstrates an exceptionally low overpotential (η_10 = 17 mV), outperforming both commercial Pt/C (27 mV) and Co_n–Pt_1@N_[6]C (56 mV) (Fig. 4a). ... overpotential at 100 mA cm⁻² is merely 93 mV ... Tafel slope (28 mV dec⁻¹) ... TOF ... 2.02 s⁻¹ ... MA value of 1.79 A mg_Pt⁻¹ ... C_dl (123 mF cm⁻²) ... negligible fluctuation of the overpotential ∼6 mV during the test for 100h (Fig. 4f).

The Co_n–Pt_1@N_[5]/[6]C-based AEMWE device only needs 1.82 V to reach an industrial current density of 1 A cm⁻² at 70 °C with a low Pt loading of ∼0.2 mg cm⁻² ... exhibits excellent stability, retaining 400 h of stable operation at 1 A cm⁻² with minimal decay (Fig. 5a, d). MA ... 0.48, 7.3, and 16.3 A mg_Pt⁻¹ at 1.5, 2.0, and 2.5 V (Fig. 5c).

nodes.description: Alkaline HER performance in 1 M KOH three-electrode system (commercial benchmark)
nodes.source_text: commercial Pt/C (27 mV) ... η_100 = 149 mV ... Pt/C (61 mV dec⁻¹) ... 20% Pt/C (0.41 s⁻¹) ... Pt/C (0.4 A mg_Pt⁻¹) ... C_dl (33 mF cm⁻²) ... overpotential increases of ∼42 mV (Fig. 4a, b, c, d, f).

nodes.characterization_summary: N 1s XPS of supports shows N_[6] (~399 eV), N_[5] (~401 eV), G-N (~402 eV), N-O (~403 eV); Co_n–N_[5]/[6]C has nearly equal N_[5]/N_[6] ratio vs N_[6]-dominant Co_n–N_[6]C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 2a, both Co_n–N_[6]C and Co_n–N_[5]/[6]C show N_[6], N_[5], graphitic nitrogen (G–N), and nitrogen oxide (N–O) at ∼399, ∼401, ∼402, and ∼403 eV in N 1s XPS spectra, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: N 1s XPS of catalysts shows metal-N (~399.5 eV) confirming Pt-N coordination; N_[5]/N_[6] proportions remain nearly unchanged after Pt coordination.
nodes.evidence_snippet: after the Pt atoms are confined, the proportions of N_[5] and N_[6] in the two systems remain nearly unchanged, while the formation of metal–N (~399.5 eV) confirms Pt–N coordination.

nodes.characterization_summary: N K-edge EELS line scan across Pt_1 shows peaks at 401 eV (N_[5]/G-N) and 410 eV (N_[6]); equal intensities in Co_n–Pt_1@N_[5]/[6]C vs N_[6]-dominant in Co_n–Pt_1@N_[6]C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The N K-edge EELS line scanning profiles across supported Pt_1 in both Co_n–Pt_1@N_[5]/[6]C and Co_n–Pt_1@N_[6]C show two prominent peaks... One peak at approximately 401 eV... while the other peak located at about 410 eV is commonly assigned to N_[6].

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt L₃-edge XANES shows negative edge shift and lower white line intensity for Co_n–Pt_1@N_[5]/[6]C vs Co_n–Pt_1@N_[6]C, indicating lower Pt oxidation state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Co_n–Pt_1@N_[5]/[6]C exhibits a more negative edge shift and a lower white line peak intensity compared to that of Co_n–Pt_1@N_[6]C, corresponding to the lower Pt oxidation states.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt L₃-edge FT-EXAFS shows Pt-N peak at ~1.9 Å (CN~4); Pt-N bond length 2.26 Å in Co_n–Pt_1@N_[5]/[6]C vs 2.25 Å in Co_n–Pt_1@N_[6]C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: both Co_n–Pt_1@N_[5]/[6]C and Co_n–Pt_1@N_[6]C show a significant peak (∼1.9 Å), corresponding to the Pt–N bond (coordination number, CN~4).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM reveals polyhedral morphology retained from ZIF precursor after pyrolysis and Pt coordination.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SEM images reveal that the polyhedral shape of the core–shell ZIF-8@ZIF-67 are well retained after thermal treatment.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows interior collapse in Co_n–Pt_1@N_[5]/[6]C vs intact structure in Co_n–Pt_1@N_[6]C; Co_n loosely embedded in open carbon nanocages vs tightly enveloped by carbon layers.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the interior of Co_n–Pt_1@N_[5]/[6]C shows significant collapse compared to Co_n–Pt_1@N_[6]C... Co_n is tightly enveloped by carbon layers in Co_n–Pt_1@N_[6]C, while it is loosely embedded within open carbon nanocages.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM reveals homogeneous Co_n distribution (~20 nm) and individual Pt single atoms closely scattered around Co_n in both catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 3e–f shows homogenous Co_n in both Co_n–Pt_1@N_[5]/[6]C and Co_n–Pt_1@N_[6]C... High-resolution HAADF-STEM images reveal individual Pt atoms coexisting with Co_n in both the systems.

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM-EDS mapping confirms more hollow carbon nanocages around Co_n in Co_n–Pt_1@N_[5]/[6]C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: STEM-EDS mapping indicates more hollow carbon nanocages around Co_n in Co_n–Pt_1@N_[5]/[6]C.

nodes.characterization_summary: Specific surface areas: Co_n–N_[5]/[6]C (600.7 m² g⁻¹) >> Co_n–N_[6]C (144.36 m² g⁻¹); both reduced after Pt confinement.
nodes.evidence_snippet: although both exhibit reduced specific surface areas due to effective Pt confinement, Co_n–N_[5]/[6]C demonstrates a significantly higher specific surface area (600.7 m² g⁻¹) compared to Co_n–N_[6]C (144.36 m² g⁻¹).

nodes.characterization_summary: Electrochemical double-layer capacitance C_dl = 123 mF cm⁻² for Co_n–Pt_1@N_[5]/[6]C vs 56 mF cm⁻² for Co_n–Pt_1@N_[6]C and 33 mF cm⁻² for Pt/C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The higher electrochemical double-layer capacitance (C_dl) value of Co_n–Pt_1@N_[5]/[6]C (123 mF cm⁻²) than that of Pt/C (33 mF cm⁻²) and Co_n–Pt_1@N_[6]C (56 mF cm⁻²).
